whatFailed: POST /api/v2/envelope/get-many with the exact body the Documents API guide publishes, {"envelopeIds": [id, id]}, is rejected with 400 Input validation failed because the endpoint's real input is a nested selector object under `ids`, so the documented batch-read call cannot work as printed.

docClaim.quote: Retrieve multiple documents by their IDs in a single request. POST /envelope/get-many ... | `envelopeIds` | array | Yes | Array of document IDs | ... curl -X POST "https://app.documenso.com/api/v2/envelope/get-many" -H "Authorization: api_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "envelopeIds": ["envelope_abc123", "envelope_def456", "envelope_ghi789"] }'
docClaim.section: Get Multiple Documents (#get-multiple-documents), Request Body + Code Examples; snapshot at .truecourse/specs/sources/docs.documenso.com/docs/developers/api/documents.md lines 690-735

observed: Steps 1 and 2 minted two envelopes from the seed template (envelope_dhbduzeshridkmkv, envelope_nytlatnoekemzehf, both 200). Step 3 posted {"envelopeIds":[...]} and got 400 with {"message":"Input validation failed","code":"BAD_REQUEST","data":{"path":"envelope.getMany"},"issues":[{"code":"invalid_type","expected":"object","received":"undefined","path":["ids"],"message":"Required"}]}. The `envelopeIds` key was ignored entirely; zod complained that the required object property `ids` was missing. server.stderr.txt is empty, so nothing crashed; this is plain input validation.
impact: Any developer who copies the published curl or TypeScript snippet gets a hard 400 and no hint of the real body; the documented batch-read is unusable as written and the correct nested selector shape is undiscoverable from the guide. No data loss, no security exposure.

rootCause.explanation: The product side is correct and deliberate. packages/trpc/server/envelope-router/get-envelopes-by-ids.types.ts lines 16-33 define ZGetEnvelopesByIdsRequestSchema as z.object({ ids: ZEnvelopeIdsSchema }) where ZEnvelopeIdsSchema is a discriminated union on `type` with variants envelopeId (string[]), documentId (number[]) and templateId (number[]), each 1 to 20 ids. get-envelopes-by-ids.ts destructures `ids` from the input and passes it straight to the lib service, and packages/app-tests/e2e/api/v2/test-unauthorized-api-access.spec.ts (lines 2900-3070) exercises the endpoint successfully with data: { ids: { type: 'envelopeId', ids: [...] } }, so the union exists to let one endpoint address envelopes by envelope id or by legacy numeric document/template id after the envelope migration. There is no `envelopeIds` key on this route at all. The documentation page invents one: the field table and both code samples name a flat `envelopeIds` array, which zod discards as an unknown key, leaving the required `ids` undefined. The guess is a plausible one because sibling routes in the same router really do take a flat envelopeIds array (bulk-cancel-envelopes.types.ts, bulk-delete-envelopes.types.ts, bulk-move-envelopes.types.ts all declare envelopeIds: string[]), and the pre-envelope /document/get-many took a flat documentIds: number[] (packages/trpc/server/document-router/get-documents-by-ids.types.ts lines 16-18). The guide also omits the response shape ({ data: [...] }, which is what the scenario asserted) and describes the field as "Array of document IDs" while the examples use envelope_ string ids. The two docs surfaces disagree with each other: the same page's top callout points readers at the OpenAPI reference, and that reference is machine-generated from the zod schema (packages/trpc/server/open-api.ts, served at /api/v2/openapi.json), so it publishes the correct `ids` selector while the hand-written guide publishes the fabricated one.

colleagueFinding.note: None of the researcher's 8 itemized Documenso findings covers /envelope/get-many; this is a ninth, separate one. It does fit their headline pattern of defects independently confirmed by community PRs left unmerged for about two weeks: PR #3135 sits in the very same ephraimduncan docs stack as #3133 (the rate-limit docs PR the coordinator already established) and #3136 (their findings 1 and 4). It also refines their finding 4 in kind: both are the hand-written Documents API guide disagreeing with the zod-generated wire contract, one on coordinate types, this one on the request body shape.

notes: For the doc author: the fix is to replace the field table and both code samples with { "ids": { "type": "envelopeId", "ids": ["envelope_abc123", ...] } }, note the 1 to 20 id cap and the documentId/templateId numeric variants, and add the { "data": [ ... ] } response section that the page currently omits. Worth flagging the inconsistency to the API owners as well: get-many is the odd one out in the envelope router, since bulk-cancel, bulk-delete and bulk-move all take a flat envelopeIds: string[] at top level, so the docs error is the natural mistake to make. The docs page carries its own hedge ('This guide may not reflect the latest endpoints or parameters, see the OpenAPI Reference'), which reduces but does not remove the harm: the page still presents a complete copy-pasteable curl that cannot succeed. The scenario itself is well formed, it sent exactly what the doc prints and asserted only that two rows come back, so no test change is warranted.
